name: Internship
description: Provides an opportunity for students to gain real-world industry working experience by practicing computing techniques such as system analysis, design, implementation, testing, and maintenance. Helps develop professional interpersonal interaction and soft communication skills within a corporate environment. Requires a final written reflective summary document.
assessment: 100% Continuous Assessment and Internship Report (Graded as Pass/Fail based on WIE supervisor site visits, company feedback, and the final written report submission)

name: Experiential Learning
description: Fosters a dynamic learning environment extending beyond traditional campus boundaries through structured local work experience and non-local learning activities. Students choose from multiple tracking tracks such as a 6-month local internship combined with a 1-week non-local study activity, or a 2-month outbound exchange alongside an 8-week local placement. Focuses on system analysis, design, implementation, testing, maintenance, and global cross-cultural communication workspace skills.
assessment: 100% Continuous Assessment and report/certificates (Graded strictly on a Pass/Fail basis by an Academic Advisor based on regular progress evaluation and completion of host organization records; does not impact graduation GPA calculations)

name: Theory of Computation
description: Provides foundational concepts in the theory of computation, focusing on the analysis and design of automata, regular expressions, context-free grammars, pushdown automata, and Turing machines. Covers computability, decidability, the Church-Turing thesis, the halting problem, reduction techniques, and intractable problems (P vs NP and NP-completeness).
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Mid-Term/Tests) and 70% Examination

name: E-Commerce Technology and Applications
description: Provides a comprehensive understanding of the technical and business infrastructure components supporting e-commerce systems. Covers applied cryptographic technology, web security protocols (SSL/TLS, firewalls, IPSec), internet payment services (credit cards, mobile payments, blockchain, cryptocurrencies), and advanced topics like recommendation algorithms, Web3, NFTs, and the metaverse.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Group Project, In-class Quizzes) and 70% Examination

name: Game Design and Development
description: Equips students with the analytical, design, and practical programming skills needed to develop 2D and 3D digital games and interactive extended reality applications. Covers real-time rendering pipelines, interactive visual effects, event loops, animation, collision detection, game physics, game AI (pathfinding, decision trees, finite state machines), multi-user game networking, and the cultural impacts of digital entertainment.
assessment: 55% Continuous Assessment (45% Major Project, 10% Mid-term Programming Exam) and 45% Final Examination

name: Business Process and Workflow Management
description: Presents a process-oriented view of business modeling and the application of workflow management systems to modern business process engineering. Focuses on workflow standards (OMG, WfMC), BPMN modeling, process discovery, life cycle stages, simulation techniques, qualitative and quantitative performance analysis, and Coloured Petri Nets modeling.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Project Written Report and Oral Presentation) and 70% Examination

name: Operations Research and Logistics Management
description: Introduces technical problems in the logistics industry and operational supply chains, teaching mathematical techniques and algorithms to solve logistics problems. Topics include transportation models, vehicle routing, path scheduling, bin packing, inventory cost models, network flow optimization (maximum flow, minimum cost flow), linear/non-linear forecasting, optimal facility placement, and RFID application specifications.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments and/or Project) and 70% Examination

name: Information Systems Audit and Control
description: Explores audit and control aspects of information management, risk assessment, and cybersecurity in project management frameworks. Covers top management control frameworks (CobiT, COSO, ISO27001), boundary, input/output, and application processing controls, computer-assisted audit techniques for evidence collection, risk methodologies, business continuity planning, disaster recovery, and advanced AI applications in cybersecurity and anti-money-laundering.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Tests and/or Project) and 70% Examination

name: Information Retrieval
description: Provides foundation knowledge in information retrieval and computational search problems. Covers Boolean and fuzzy Boolean retrieval, vector space models, term weighting schemes, cosine similarity measures, query processing and expansion, inverted file index construction, dict management, text clustering algorithms (k-means, hierarchical), and web spidering or hyperlink link analysis.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Lab Exercises, and Project) and 70% Examination

name: Biometrics and Security
description: Covers underlying e-security technologies including digital watermarking, data authentication, and cryptography principles like conventional encryption, block ciphers (DES), public-key cryptography, hash functions, and digital signatures. Introduces biometric computing methods for physical (fingerprint, palmprint, iris, face) and behavioral (voice, signature, gait) human identification, evaluating system error rates across multi-biometric applications.
prerequisites: (AMA1104 Introductory Probability or HKDSE Maths Extended Module or equivalent) & (COMP3422 Creative Digital Media Design or equivalent)
assessment: 60% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Lab exercises, Project, Mid-term) and 40% Examination

name: Programming Fundamentals
description: Introduces fundamental elements of computer programming and basic techniques necessary for developing sophisticated application programs. Topics include computation and interpretation, elementary programming constructs, selection, repetition, functions, structures, lists, sets, strings, problem-solving, testing, and debugging.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Quizzes, Individual projects) and 70% Final Examination

name: Programming Fundamentals and Applications
description: Provides knowledge on the fundamental elements in computer programming and introduces its application in solving practical problems across different domains. Topics cover basic concepts of computing, I/O and flow control, data collection (sequences, lists, tuples, sets, strings, dictionaries), file operations, modular design, sorting and searching, NumPy arrays and matrices, and data manipulation in R.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Quizzes, Project) and 70% Final Examination

name: Data Structures
description: Introduces basic concepts of data structures and algorithms, teaching students how to apply them in computer programs. Topics include abstract data types, linear structures (linked-lists, stacks, queues), tree structures (binary trees, balanced trees), common data structures (priority queues, heaps), basic and advanced sorting (bubble, insertion, selection, quicksort, mergesort, heapsort), and searching (sequential, binary, tree search, dictionary, hashing).
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (assignments / project / quizzes) and 70% Final Examination

name: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Introduces data structures and algorithms, focusing on solving computational problems efficiently. Topics cover asymptotic notations, efficiency analysis, linear and tree structures, greedy and divide-and-conquer sorting algorithms, heapsort, priority queues, hashing collision resolution, graphs (representations, DFS, BFS), algorithmic design techniques (greedy, dynamic programming, divide-and-conquer, recursion), and practical program development.
assessment: 60% Continuous Assessment (15% Written Assignments, 20% Programming Assignments, 25% Quizzes) and 40% Examination

name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
description: Provides in-depth knowledge on algorithm design techniques and advanced algorithms for various data types. Covers mathematical analysis techniques, big-O notation, recurring relations, advanced design (dynamic programming, divide-and-conquer, branch-and-bound, greedy algorithms), advanced analysis (randomised algorithms, probabilistic/amortised analysis), computational geometry (range searching, convex hull, closest pairs), and NP-complete problems.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Mid-Term / Tests) and 70% Examination

name: Algorithms Engineering
description: Focuses on designing and implementing algorithms for real-life computational problems like vehicle routing, route searching, graph partitioning, and near-neighbor search. Covers considerations of data characteristics, problem requirements (response time, memory consumption, solution quality), performance profiling, performance bottlenecks, implementation options (library functions, compiler optimization, multi-threading, vectorized code/SIMD), and performance measurement experiments.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (assignments, project, quizzes) and 70% Final Exam

name: Human Computer Interaction
description: Explores theoretical and practical issues in human factors for designing human-computer interfaces. Topics include human information processing (perception, memory limits, mental models, metaphors), visual perception, computer graphics and multimodal interfaces, dialogue interaction techniques, prototyping and user-centered design, physical/cognitive ergonomics, I/O devices, evaluation standards, metric design, and experiment statistics.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments and/or Project) and 70% Final Examination

name: Artificial Intelligence
description: Introduces fundamental concepts, history, and technical trends of artificial intelligence, alongside problem formulation and intelligent algorithms. Covers agent design, rationality, knowledge-based agents, forward/backward chaining inference, Bayesian networks, uninformed/informed search strategies, heuristics, local searches (hill-climbing, simulated annealing, genetic algorithms), constraint satisfaction, supervised/unsupervised/reinforcement learning, decision trees, SVM, neural networks, and AI ethics.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (project, lab exercises, quizzes) and 70% Final Examination

name: Discrete Mathematics
description: Introduces concepts and applications of discrete mathematical structures to build fundamental reasoning skills for upper-level computing subjects. Topics cover sets, relations, functions, equivalence, cardinality, propositional and predicate logic, truth tables, tautologies, mathematical induction, counting techniques, pigeonhole principle, graphs, planar graphs, graph colouring, trees, minimum spanning trees, network flows, and combinatorial circuits.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments and Quizzes) and 70% Examination

name: Mathematics for Machine Learning
description: Provides fundamental concepts of mathematics necessary for machine learning and optimization algorithms. Topics include vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, matrix decompositions (eigenvalues, singular values), pseudo-inverses, discrete/continuous probability distributions (Gaussian), maximum likelihood estimation, Bayes' rule, least squares, one-dimensional/constrained/convex optimization, gradient descent, and stochastic gradient descent using NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, and PyTorch.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments and Quizzes) and 70% Examination

name: E-Business
description: Introduces fundamental concepts, technologies, and system design structures in the digital e-business enterprise. Covers internet/intranet/extranet business models, languages for the web, XML data integration, software agents, front-end and backend computing infrastructures, network/data security protocols, authentication, public-key encryption, digital money, online payment architectures, web database system integration, and global e-business applications via the business model canvas.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Tutor Exercises, Mid-term Quizzes) and 70% Examination

name: Computer Networking
description: Acquires a foundational understanding of computer communications technologies and network architectures with primary emphasis on the link layer and above. Topics cover data encapsulation, OSI reference model, TCP/IP reference model, performance evaluation, framing, error detection, automatic repeat request (ARQ) protocols, LAN, MAC protocols, connectionless/connection-oriented network layers, distance-vector/link-state routing algorithms, IP addressing, subnets, ARP, UDP, TCP, socket programming, and client-server IP applications.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Project) and 70% Examination

name: Database Systems
description: Focuses on the principles and practices of database design, analysis, application implementation, and database administration. Topics cover DBMS architectures, data independence, entity-relationship (ER) modeling, functional dependencies, normalization, relational algebra, relational calculus, structured query language (SQL), embedded SQL, physical file organizations, indexing and hashing, estimation of query-processing costs, buffer management, transaction processing, concurrency control, crash recovery, security, and web databases.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Tests and Projects) and 70% Examination

name: Computer Organization
description: Provides introductory but comprehensive knowledge on computer systems, computer organization, computer system architecture, and assembly language programming. Topics include basic clock synchronization, instruction cycles, computer arithmetic (binary, signed integers, octal, hex, BCD, floating-point representations), CPU internal structure, reduced instruction set computers (RISC), assembler commands, logic gates, flip-flops, main memory (RAM, ROM), I/O system interrupts, standard bus interfaces, cache memory, and virtual memory.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (20% Quiz & Programming Assignments, 10% Mid-Term) and 70% Examination

name: Operating Systems
description: Introduces services, internal structures, concepts, theories, and implementation issues of modern operating systems using Unix and Linux as core examples. Topics cover shell scripting, system calls, kernel structures, interrupts, process control (creation, termination, scheduling), concurrent processes, inter-process communication (IPC), critical section problems, synchronization, deadlocks, address translation, memory allocation, paging and segmentation, virtual memory, file systems, secondary storage, capabilities, and security threats.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Quizzes, Project) and 70% Examination

name: Social and Collaborative Computing
description: Explores specialised concepts, history, design principles, and behaviors behind modern social networks and collaborative computing systems. Topics cover blogging, collaborative filtering, Internet search algorithms, social media platforms, Web 2.0 architectures, virtual communities, online credibility, motivations and social psychology, social attributes of nodes/networks, online social network modeling, data collection/trending, social network marketing, business models, intellectual property, and user privacy/security.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Projects, Reports, Tests) and 70% Final Examination

name: Business Intelligence and Customer Relationship Management
description: Provides an understanding of the key components of business intelligence (BI) and customer relationship management (CRM) frameworks within e-commerce environments. Topics include consumer behaviour analysis, customer profitability profiling, brand and channel strategy planning, data warehousing, integrated eCRM solutions, software packages, personalisation, and loyalty program metrics.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Tests and/or Project) and 70% Examination

name: Software Engineering
description: Familiarises students with theories, concepts, and engineering methodologies across the software development lifecycle. Covers traditional software process models, agile software development techniques, requirements engineering (elicitation, specification, validation), system context and structural modeling, architectural design patterns, object-oriented lifecycle analysis, test-driven development (TDD), and system evolution/legacy maintenance.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Project) and 70% Examination

name: Computer Systems Security
description: Equips students with foundational knowledge of security threats to computer systems and software interfaces. Covers security policies, classical and modern symmetric/public-key cryptography, key agreement and password authentication protocols, software exploits (such as buffer overflow and memory corruption), principles of secure coding, code audit, web security principles, input validation, blockchain infrastructure, and malware remediation.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of modern operating systems is preferred
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Quizzes, Project) and 70% Examination

name: Database Security
description: Introduces security vulnerabilities and mitigation measures specific to core database applications and infrastructures. Covers relational architectures (MySQL, Oracle) alongside distributed models, database authorization mechanisms (discretionary and mandatory access control), file system security protocols, disk encryption, inference control in statistical databases, SQL injection attack defenses, database auditing, and searchable encryption implementations.
prerequisites: COMP2411 or equivalent introductory database subject
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment, 70% Examination

name: Web Application Design and Development
description: Explores principles, infrastructure, and technical design models behind modern distributed web applications. Covers two-tier and multi-tier database-driven internet architectures, full-stack client-side and server-side programming frameworks using JavaScript/TypeScript, React, and Node.js, asynchronous communication protocols (AJAX, Fetch API, WebSockets), single-page and progressive web applications, and cloud-hosted deployment.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Tests & Projects) and 70% Examination

name: Creative Digital Media Design
description: Provides core foundation knowledge regarding multimedia computing principles, data representation formats, and creative digital system design. Covers media streaming characteristics, signal compression standards, human visual/audio information processing systems, perception and cognitive limits, entropy/hybrid coding techniques, speech analysis tools, image rendering, and current technical trends in the multimedia industry.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Project, Quizzes, Midterms) and 70% Examination

name: System Programming
description: Teaches practical approaches and theoretical structures needed to design system-level software with advanced OS kernels. Topics include UNIX file architecture representations, device driver interfaces and internal operations, parent/child process lifecycle management, C-based system calls, and compiler construction essentials including lexical token recognition via Finite Automata, context-free top-down parsing, and intermediate code generation.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Assignments) and 70% Examination

name: Legal Aspects and Ethics of Computing
description: Explores security responsibilities, compliance guidelines, and professional integrity frameworks for computing practitioners. Topics cover cybercrime legislation, hacker ethics, generative AI fraud controls, data privacy ordinances (including GDPR compliance), intellectual property rights systems across Hong Kong, US, and China, standard management practices (ISO 27001, ISO 42001, ISO 56005), and UN Sustainable Development Goals.
assessment: 100% Continuous Assessment (Assignments, Tests, Projects, Presentations)

name: Information Systems Development
description: Provides orientation and practical skills in enterprise information systems development, focusing on modern cloud-native architectures, microservices, containerised deployment, and the twelve-factor apps methodology. Covers essential software engineering and DevOps development methodologies including Git version control, branching strategies, automated testing, continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines, and various infrastructure deployment strategies (rolling, blue-green, canary). Introduces agile project planning, key metrics, and IT risk mitigation frameworks.
assessment: 30% Continuous Assessment (Exercises, Assignments, Tests and Projects) and 70% Final Examination
